thread:
Ravi: Quick RFC follow-up: thinking about a lighter-weight alternative to the deferred-shedder discussed earlier. Idea is: prewarm pacing + CPU-staging spillback. Instead of buffering many prewarm requests on the GPU queue, we briefly divert them to a CPU staging queue where we do partial warmup (encode-only or KV-prefetch) and then retry to GPU with a lower cost. Questions: viability, complexity, and how it impacts tenant isolation.

Priya: Interesting. CPU-staging could absorb bursts and avoid noisy GPU jobs. But partial warmup still costs memory and some compute. We need to quantify: encode-only latency vs full prewarm. Any numbers?

Ravi: Rough sketch: full prewarm = 40-60ms GPU job; encode-only + KV-read = 8-12ms CPU work + small indexed GPU call to attach cache (maybe 10ms). Net could be lower if we batch CPU work. Benefits: less head-of-line on GPU, avoid autoscale triggers.

Nora: Main risk = resource coupling. If we move too much to CPU staging, CPU becomes a new bottleneck and affects other control-plane tasks. Also need TTL on staged items so stale partial warms don't pile up.

Ben: Can we make staging optional per-tenant? e.g., high-tier get direct prewarm, low-tier go via CPU-staging. That aligns incentives and avoids one tenant hogging. Also fewer knobs globally.

Ravi: Yes — per-tenant policy is planned. We'll expose admission policy: direct_preheat, staged_preheat, immediate_shed. Default: staged_preheat for mid/low tiers.

Priya: Observability needs: staged_queue_length, staged_retry_rate, staged_age_histogram, gpu_prewarm_count, p99_latency_unrelated. We should also instrument partial-warm success rate (did staged item succeed when retried).

Nora: Another thought: token-aware admission. If request is small (few tokens) maybe cost of prewarm is disproportionate; prefer shedding. For large requests that benefit from warm context, prioritize. That reduces unnecessary warms.

Ben: Agree. Simple heuristic: expected_remaining_tokens * token_warm_cost > warmup_threshold -> attempt prewarm. Need a cheap estimator at admission.

Ravi: Implementation plan (mini):
1) Add CPU-staging queue + retry logic with TTL (200-500ms).
2) Admission policy per-tenant + global staging cap.
3) Token-aware estimator at admission.
4) Dashboards and FF.

Priya: We should simulate before rollout. I'll adapt the micro-sim I used for packing to model CPU staging service times, GPU prewarm costs, and autoscaler reaction. Key outputs: p50/p99 unrelated latency, staging overflow events, cost delta.

Nora: Rollout: feature-flagged, start at 0.5% traffic (edge cases often show up even at small %). Create canary probes that generate cold-shard workloads and measure interference. Revert thresholds: p99_unrelated +10% or staged_retry_rate > 30% for 5m.

Ben: Also add a cheap quality probe: warm-success vs fallback-quality since staged warms might fail and fall back to cheaper model or degrade quality. Track quality_regression_by_tenant.

Ravi: Good. For knobs I propose: staged_ttl_ms=300, global_staged_cap=100 per GPU, per_tenant_staged_tokens=250, token_warm_threshold=80. Conservative defaults so we don't change much.

Priya: I'll run sim with staged_ttl in [100,300,500], cap in [50,100,200], and token_threshold in [40,80,160]. Will post graphs.

DeployBot: Perf sim started: https://perf.redwood.internal/sim/633123 - job 633123 queued. ETA 90m :robot_face:

Nora: Thanks. I'll draft the FF text and a short runbook with revert conditions. Also add a note to ops to watch autoscaler churn during the canary.

Ben: One more corner: interaction with KV-eviction. If staged items hold references, they may delay eviction. Force staged items to not pin long-lived handles. Use weak refs or prefetch-only tokens.

Ravi: Noted. We'll design staging objects to be ephemeral and not hold strong cache pins.

Priya: OK I will update the sim and link results here when ready. If sims look good, we can land metrics PR behind FF and run canary next week.

Ravi: Perfect. Meeting follow-up: publish the small experiment doc and tag infra + SRE. Next sync in 48h or when sim results are in.
